title: Sycophancy Steering x Reward-Model Gaming: Can a Steered Model Better Fool an Evaluator?

original_idea.body: Sycophancy steering may inflate LLM-judge scores without improving correctness - steering as a reward-hacking lever against an evaluator.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to evaluator-manipulation/reward-hacking, a recognized fuzzy-reward safety pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited CAA methodology plus LLM-judge scoring; executable by novice with mentor on a single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single clean experiment: steer sycophancy, score with judge vs ground truth, measure decoupling.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fuzzy-reward evaluator-manipulation is a neglected, lab-deprioritized model-organism area needing no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on open model and open judge; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Sycophancy inflating judge scores is plausibly studied; the steering-as-lever framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sycophancy and LLM-judge bias are studied; using a steering vector as the reward-hacking lever may be partly open.
